quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is a common sign of a drunk driver?

options.text: They are weaving between lanes.
They are driving slower than other traffic.
They are making quick, sudden stops.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving between lanes, driving slower than traffic, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: On a long trip, how can you avoid getting tired?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break to avoid fatigue. If you get drowsy, pull off the road to a safe place and take a nap or stay somewhere for the night.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol while taking medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can increase the effects of both the alcohol and medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can increase the effects of both the alcohol and medicine.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other drugs can make both substances affect you more strongly. For example, one drink with cold medicine can affect you as much as several drinks would alone.

questions.question: Where can bicyclists legally ride?

options.text: On the roadway, on the shoulder, or in a bicycle lane.
On freeways and highways where signs say it is illegal.
In a left turn lane without turning, even if there is no traffic.
On the wrong side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the roadway, on the shoulder, or in a bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists can ride on the roadway, on the shoulder, in a bicycle lane, or on a sidewalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway begins.
A steep hill is ahead.
The bridge ahead has low clearance.
Two lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead has low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the bridge ahead has low clearance. Do not go through if your vehicle is taller than the height shown (in this case, 13 feet 6 inches).

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going further.
Slow down and let trains pass first.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass first.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Always slow down when you approach railroad tracks. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for them to pass.

questions.question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic lights help prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey traffic signals. However, when an officer is directing traffic, you must follow the officer's directions instead.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Never pass if an oncoming car is in the passing lane, your view is blocked by a curve or hill, at an intersection, at a railroad crossing or bridge, or in any no passing zone. Do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn allowed.
No U-turn allowed.
Truck route to the left.

questions.explanation: This sign means that left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go and keep driving safely.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off in return.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go and keep driving safely.
questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. To avoid road rage, stay calm and continue driving safely.

questions.question: When you change lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal before you change lanes or exit. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before you move.

questions.question: A seat belt should fit:

options.text: Loosely.
Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Hidden beneath the seat.
To stop the seat belt buzzer or light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable with enough room to fit your fist between it and your chest.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:

options.text: Are turning.
Have your emergency brake on.
Are changing lanes.
Are slowing down or stopping.

questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights working at all times.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention to the road.
Driving too fast for conditions.
Following other vehicles too closely.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Driving too fast causes crashes. Not paying attention can cause collisions. Following too closely causes most rear-end collisions.

questions.question: To change lanes you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal first. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one else is entering the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the road. Merge safely when it is clear.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are merely suggestions.
Must be followed only when there is traffic.
Must be followed only when police are present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: A sudden change in weather means you should change how you drive.
You should slow down in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Adjust your driving when weather changes suddenly. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections or railroad crossings.
When the road is wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, on curves, near pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: A driver taking an over-the-counter drug should:

options.text: Read the label before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Drive regardless of warning labels.
Drive only during the day.

questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings about cold and allergy medications. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure.

questions.question: What should you do to make sure your physical condition does not make you drive unsafely?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how any medicine you take affects your driving.
Only drive within what your body can handle.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects how safely you can drive. You should know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe for you to do so.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps your driving skills but hurts your judgment.
It hurts both your driving skills and your judgment.
It does not affect either your driving skills or your judgment.
It does not affect your judgment but hurts your driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It hurts both your driving skills and your judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms skills you need to drive safely. It slows your reaction time, makes it hard to see clearly, and affects how you judge speed and distance. It also makes you take more risks.

questions.question: When the traffic light is green, what should you do to make a left turn?

options.text: Let oncoming traffic pass, then turn when it is safe.
Turn quickly before oncoming traffic gets closer.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.
Only turn when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let oncoming traffic pass, then turn when it is safe.
questions.explanation: At a green light, oncoming traffic has the right-of-way. You can turn left unless a sign says you cannot, but only when it is safe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They tell you about dangers ahead. This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming, so you should be ready for a yellow or red light.

questions.question: An intersection has no signs or traffic lights. You arrive at the same time as a car to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and make the other car stop.
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two cars reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the car on the right goes first. Wait until that car passes safely before you go.
